submission.natural_language_explanation: L4/H6 is a broad retrospective single-anchor pointer: by default it parks nearly all attention on the passage-first token (a sink), where its write sits at or below floor, and mid-passage it usually sits slightly off the mean write so ordinary prose reads active-weak; when one earlier content token, typically the clause subject or topic noun and especially an orthographically salient token such as a file-start marker or non-Latin word, self-registers, the head snaps to it (weight 0.75-1.0) and re-retrieves it at the next predicate or juncture token (and, commas, prepositions, periods, line breaks), with the spike growing when the anchor lies far back in a long passage. Strength therefore tracks pointing state (sink versus anchored) and prior-context length, not the rarity of the attended token: rare-numeral passages can sit entirely at floor while common-word sentences spike, and previous-token, duplicate-token and induction scores are all near zero.
